bib.title: GLM: General Language Model Pretraining with Autoregressive Blank Infilling
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 60th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2022), Volume 1: Long Papers, pages 320-335

question: Can one pretraining framework perform best across NLU, unconditional generation and conditional generation?
hypothesis: Autoregressive blank infilling with span shuffling and 2D positional encodings unifies BERT-style, GPT-style and T5-style pretraining and beats each at equal size and data.
contributions: GLM: autoregressive blank infilling with span shuffling and 2D positional encoding
Multi-task pretraining (short spans plus document-level or sentence-level long spans) so one model handles NLU, conditional and unconditional generation
NLU classification reformulated as cloze questions (PET-style) with multi-token answers

method.summary: A single Transformer is pretrained by blanking spans (Poisson lambda=3, until 15% of tokens masked), replacing each with one [MASK], and generating the spans autoregressively in random order with 2D positions. Part A (corrupted text) is bidirectional, Part B (spans) causal. Evaluated on SuperGLUE (cloze finetuning), Gigaword, SQuAD QG, CNN/DM, XSum, Yahoo infilling, LAMBADA and BookWiki perplexity.
method.task: Pretraining by autoregressive blank infilling; finetuning for NLU as cloze, generation as Part-A context plus [MASK]

datasets.name: RoBERTa-style corpus (BookCorpus, Wikipedia 16GB, CC-News-en, OpenWebText2 66GB)
datasets.source: Stories removed (unavailable); OpenWebText replaced by OpenWebText2; CC-News replaced by CC-News-en (Mackenzie et al., 2020)

datasets.preprocessing: mask ratio 10-50%, contiguous masked tokens collapsed into one blank; dynamic masking

datasets.name: LAMBADA

models.name: BERT Base/Large, UniLM Large, T5 Base (220M)/Large (770M), BART Large, RoBERTa Large, MASS, SemQG, BERTSumAbs, UniLMv2 Base, BLM, GPT Large

other.GPT Large: trained by the authors with same data and tokenization as GLM Large

training.objective: Autoregressive blank infilling, max over theta of E_z[sum_i log p(s_zi | x_corrupt, s_z<i)] with random span permutation. Spans: Poisson lambda=3 until at least 15% masked. Multi-task: short spans and long spans sampled with equal chance in a batch; document-level = one span of 50%-100% of original length (uniform); sentence-level = full-sentence spans covering 15% of tokens.

other.410M/515M: same hyperparameters as Large except architecture, 200K steps
other.BERT comparison: BERT used batch 256 and 1,000,000 steps; GLM Large used 1024 and 200,000

inference.decoding: Seq2seq: beam search, beam size 5, repeated trigrams removed (Gigaword), length penalty tuned on dev. Text samples: top-k random sampling k=40.
inference.samples: single run implied; no seeds or variance reported
inference.prompting: NLU as cloze: p(y|x) = p(v(y)|c(x)) / sum_y' p(v(y')|c(x)), finetuned with cross-entropy. Single-token tasks scored by verbalizer logit, multi-token tasks (ReCoRD, COPA, WSC) by summed log-probs.

parameters.perplexity_overlap: sliding window with overlap o=256 for all models

limits: No seeds, variances or significance tests are reported.
The authors cannot compare directly with T5 because data and parameter counts differ.
Language modeling is weaker than GPT at equal size (GLM Doc below GPT Large); needs 410M to approach it.
Due to resource limits GLM RoBERTa was trained for only 250,000 steps, half RoBERTa's.
RoBERTa corpus was reconstructed (Stories removed, OpenWebText2 and CC-News-en substituted), so not identical data.
Pretrained models were not in the supplement and were promised for later release (Appendix A.3).
Baseline BERT scores are from original papers with a different batch size and steps; own reproduction is lower (71.2 avg).
Gains over BERT on GLUE and SQuAD are smaller (Appendix C).

terms.definition: Spans of the input are replaced by a single [MASK] and regenerated autoregressively, in random span order, conditioned on the corrupted text and previous spans.
Each token has two position ids: position in the corrupted text (the [MASK] position for spans) and intra-span position (0 for Part A, 1..span length for Part B).
Part A is the corrupted text attending bidirectionally; Part B is the masked spans, attending to A and earlier B tokens.
Mapping of labels to answer words of the cloze question.

figures.caption: GLM pretraining. (a) The original text is [x1..x6]. Two spans [x3] and [x5, x6] are sampled. (b) Replace the sampled spans with [M] in Part A, and shuffle the spans in Part B. (c) GLM autoregressively generates Part B. Each span is prepended with [S] as input and appended with [E] as output. 2D positional encoding represents inter- and intra-span positions. (d) Self-attention mask.
